vp5_ruling.text: 2026-10-10T10:25:02Z [pyt-axis-lead] V-P5 RULING (POST HOC, made by the lead with the category known): the 163 pair-level float and 3 section-D verdict mismatches between implementations E and I are float64 rounding of two GPU kernels (max 9.1e-14 absolute, on debiased-CKA thresholds and null means near zero); every integer, p, decision, category and modifier agrees, R = E and R = I with 0 mismatches, and no order, censoring or tie changes (smallest decision gap 6.9e-8). V-P5 is accepted with an added absolute tolerance of 1e-12 on CKA floats; no code or output changes.

paper_sentences_s13.rule: plan section 13: frozen sentence of the realised category; wording that departs from it is labelled post hoc
paper_sentences_s13.abstract_clause_C: On seven Pythia models, where a confirmatory test was fixed before any Pythia weight was downloaded, calibration kept the trend, which moved from $+0.93$ to $+0.89$.
paper_sentences_s13.sec_exp_aggregation_paragraph_C: Three sizes leave each of these outcomes at $p\ge1/6$, so we added a confirmatory test on the seven Pythia models from 70M to 6.9B, trained on the same data in the same order \citep{biderman2023pythia}. Single-model features again predicted thresholds rising with size, and the thresholds lay in the predicted band for seven of the seven models. The raw scores rose faster, by a median $0.024$ per doubling of parameters against $0.0063$ for the thresholds, so calibration moved the layer-max CKA trend only from $0.93$ to $0.89$, an outcome allowed by Corollary~\ref{cor:aggregation}.
paper_sentences_s13.limitations_C: Each size trend rests on one draw of evaluation inputs, and the one confirmatory family, Pythia, keeps the layer-max CKA trend under calibration, while the other families give exact one-sided $p$ of at least $1/120$ and $1/6$.
